landing.title: Which reporting duties apply to your company?
landing.intro: Germany, Austria and Switzerland have introduced new cyber-incident reporting regimes (NIS2UmsuCG, NISG 2024, ISG). We automatically assess which regimes apply to you, which thresholds are relevant, and where your public-facing security gaps are – in under three minutes, no login required.

result.none_relevant: No regime was flagged as relevant based on the country of main establishment alone. Check subsidiaries and sector via the free scan if needed.
result.limits_body: This triage was generated automatically from your incident intake and the versioned YAML rules (NIS2UmsuCG, NISG, ISG). Absolute deadlines are calculated from the stated time of discovery. Without sector and size data the home regime often remains **unclear** – that is intentional. Significance triggers (availability, personal data, scale) come from each rules file. This is a first orientation and **not legal advice**. When in doubt, contact counsel and the competent authority immediately.

items.q: Does NIS2 / NISG / ISG apply to my company?
items.a: It depends on sector, size and structure — thresholds differ across Germany, Austria and Switzerland. NexusScope checks your profile against each regime and states Confirmed, Likely, Needs review, or Insufficient information, including what remains open.

NexusScope provides regulatory readiness intelligence based on referenced public sources. Results are intended to support internal assessment and should be reviewed by qualified legal or compliance professionals where appropriate. NexusScope does not replace lawyers, auditors, or regulators.
Your data is stored in Switzerland and the EU, used to produce your report and to notify you about early access. Scans use public sources only, honour robots.txt, and never access protected systems.
Waitlist onboarding for early access is open now. Join and we will notify you when your company can run its first scan.

items.q: What does a public-footprint check include?
items.a: Passive DNS, TLS and HTTP-header observations on the domain you provide, plus published pages where reachable. GET requests only, no credentials, no port scans. Findings are limited to what is visible from public sources.

items.q: What do Confirmed, Likely, Needs review and Insufficient information mean?
items.a: Confirmed: the stated profile meets (or clearly misses) the cited thresholds. Likely: strong signals, but a nuance remains. Needs review: evidence points both ways or a classification step is unfinished. Insufficient information: required inputs are missing — the report lists what would resolve it instead of guessing.
